entries.text: Added a button-press animation for light switches and elevator buttons: the light toggles the moment the finger lands, and the off hand presses while you hold a weapon.
Fixed bare bulbs and ceiling light tubes looking solid when switched off: the glass is now see-through.

releases.title: The Durham food range, tea and strawberries

entries.text: Added strawberries to grow in planters, strawberry jam, and cups of tea brewed at the coffee machine.
Changed the food range to the Durham set: 70 old snacks, drinks, meals, crops and medical items are gone, and recipes, loot and vending machines use what is left.
Changed tomatoes and baked potatoes to new models.

Fixed switched-off lights looking wrong: bulbs are frosted white instead of turquoise, the tripod floor lamp keeps its fabric shade, and ceiling light panels look like a white diffuser instead of dark metal.

releases.title: Storage you open, furniture you drag

entries.text: Added a hardware drawer for screws and dowels, a plank rack and a cardboard rack: each holds only its own material, twenty at a time.
Added a digital wristwatch beside the catalogue that shows the store day and time, your health and your stamina.
Added clickable divider tabs to the catalogue, which turn straight to their department.
Added a two-handed overhead slam: press both attack buttons together, and hold them to charge it like a punch. It hits twice as hard as a single punch.
Added a flourish on X: with the hammer out, it spins or inspects it on demand, and other players see it too.

Added a stamina cost to punches and melee swings: every strike you actually throw uses some stamina, and a swing cut off before it lands costs nothing. With too little stamina left the strike still comes out, but weaker and slower, so charged blows are the efficient way to fight.
Added a full animation set for the hammer: it is drawn and put away by hand, spun the first time you pick it up, and now and then spun or inspected while you stand still holding it.

Added a wind-up to punches: hold the attack button to charge a harder punch, up to double damage, and the charge carries into the follow-up punch. Release early to throw it sooner, or hold at full charge until the arm starts to strain and the punch lets fly on its own.
Added controller map controls: the right stick pans the map and the triggers zoom smoothly, and Y places a ping.
Added mild aim assist for controllers: the camera turns a little slower while your crosshair is over an enemy. It can be turned off in the controller settings.
Added PlayStation button icons, shown whenever a PlayStation controller is in use.
Added a pointer speed slider to the controller settings.
Added controller vibration for hits, landed swings, explosions and station work, with an option to turn it off in the controller settings.
Added the Steam on-screen keyboard for text fields when playing with a controller on Steam Deck or in Big Picture.
Added full controller support to every screen: the left stick moves a pointer that leans toward anything you can click, A clicks, X right-clicks and the bumpers switch tabs or bags.
Added a Grab key (C) for taking hold of furniture and dragging it about. By default one press grabs and the next lets go; a setting switches it to hold-to-grab.
Added cooking in the microwave and oven: put up to three things on the tray, shut the door and press Cook; the food comes back cooked on the tray when the timer runs out.
Added a stand mixer bench that works flour and bottled water into dough.
Added a furniture showroom level that spawns the mid-century kitchen, shelves, bookcases, racks and seating on a grid with a carpet of loose items beside them.
Added pull-out drawers to the filing cabinet and sideboard, and a drop-down flap on the filing cabinet; the filing cabinet's bottom drawer slides out when its storage opens.
Added storage to the bike rack and the umbrella stand. The rack takes flattened cardboard and the stand takes planks of wood, eight apiece.
Added working doors and drawers on the mid-century fridges, oven, microwave and console: drag them open or shut, and they stay where you leave them until dragged again.
Added a working dishwasher: its door drops open and the bottom rack slides out to load it.
Added an old copper compass in the top corner that shows the map around you under its glass.
Added four hand-animated pickups that play at random when grabbing an item; with a weapon or tool in hand, only the left hand reaches while the right keeps its grip.
Added a cold bag carried alongside the basket for food; the basket refuses food and fridges take nothing else.
Added storage on the furniture itself: opening a shelf, fridge or drawer swings the camera over, sets the basket beside it, and stacks move between the two by hand or with Take all and Put all.

Added the shopping-basket bag: items sit in it as real objects on a hidden grid, each with its own footprint. Click to pick up a stack, right-click to take or drop one at a time, and release outside the basket to drop it on the floor.
Added four hooks on the front of the basket for weapons, and a click on a loose item on the floor brings it into the basket.
Added a Weapon Slots tab between the basket and the cold bag: weapons on the basket hooks only move while that tab is open, and the camera swings down to the hooks.
Added map waypoints: middle- or right-click on the map to place one at the right floor height, and click it again to remove it. Pings on the map are coloured by type.
Added a parachute backpack: with it equipped, hold jump while falling to drift down slowly and land safely.
Added settings to turn off the camera coil, the widening view and the controller hum while a punch charges.
Added a hands-on sewing machine: drag scrap fabric onto the bed under the needle, turn the stitch dial, and walk the marker round the ring to feed the seam through.
Added a character builder to the Staff File: build, face, complexion, hair and facial hair, shown on a full-screen turntable you can drag to any angle.
Added separate top, bottom, shoe and headwear picks, so any shirt goes with any trousers and the caps and sun hats can be worn on their own.
Added a picture of every garment on its wardrobe tile, including going barefoot or bare-headed.
Added a wardrobe of six outfits, streetwear and formalwear with real jackets, shirts, shorts, boots and trainers, each fitted to both builds.
Added a Staff File screen to the main menu for choosing who you play as, and your choice follows you into other people's stores.

Added a small soft dot above nearby furniture that opens a screen (crafting and production benches, planters, shops; storage is left alone); it hides while the piece is being dragged or is still settling.
Added vending machines to the stores: world generation can now place them.
Changed the arms to swing with your stride when your hands are empty, instead of hanging stiffly at your sides.
Changed Previous on the catalogue's first page to close the book back to its front cover.
Changed the catalogue to list your objectives and turn with Previous and Next buttons, so your goals live in one place.
Changed the flashlight to hold off while the catalogue is held up, so the pages read by their own lamp rather than being washed out, and the beam comes back when you put the book away.
Changed the character preview to fill the whole stage instead of standing in a narrow portrait strip down the middle of it.
Changed drag-to-rotate on the character preview to turn the figure the way you drag, like pushing a turntable.
Changed punches to land with weight, with the fist giving on contact, a small camera jolt, controller rumble, a whoosh on every swing and a heavier sound on hard blows, so a hit reads as a hit.
Changed the punches to a right cross followed by a left, both thrown from a raised guard.
Changed punching into a two-hit combo, so pressing again while the first punch lands flows straight into the second instead of restarting it.
Changed unarmed attacks into two separate punches that chain off each other, so a single tap throws one punch instead of committing you to a two-hit flurry.

Changed the hammer's attacks to an overhead swing on left click, a sideways swing on right click and a backhand on both together, each charged by holding the button; a swing that hits a wall now stops on it and recoils instead of fading back to idle.
Changed enemies to flinch harder from stronger punches, so a charged blow visibly rocks them back.
Changed punching so switching between attacks is instant and only repeating the same punch has to recover, so a quick one-two flows instead of stalling.

Changed controller look to be much faster by default, with turns speeding up when the stick is held all the way over, so turning around no longer drags. Controller sensitivity has been reset to the new default.

Changed the microwave and oven to keep their door shut while cooking: pulling it open stops the cook and puts the ingredients back, and food left inside for longer than it took to cook comes out as a burnt pile.
Changed the basic crafting table: put the parts on the bench, press Craft, and the result lands on the bench beside them.
Changed Upholstery Fabric and Woven Cloth to Frayed Fabric and Hemmed Fabric, both yellow with stitching on the hemmed one, so the sewing machine's input and output read apart at a glance.

Changed staff hit reactions so they flinch from the side and body part that was struck, build up a stagger bar that knocks them off balance when it fills, and shrug off hits mid-swing, so fights read as an exchange instead of a stun-lock.
Changed an enemy that is fighting you to keep fighting while it can see you; it only gives up once you are out of sight and quiet, or once you have led it far from its post.

Changed how enemies notice you, so that one distant footstep is ignored but a few in a row, a heavy landing or a crash of furniture brings them over to look, to make sneaking a matter of how much noise you make rather than whether you made any.
Changed bookcases, display shelves, ovens and counters to hold what you put in them on their own shelves and in their own drawers, so you can see what is in a piece before you open it.
Changed the chairs, sofas, fridges, counters and microwaves over to the mid-century set; fridges keep food behind a door that swings open with the storage screen.

Changed storage and benches that open a close-up view: when a wall or other furniture leaves no room for the camera, the prompt greys out and says "Blocked: no room to look" instead of opening onto the wall.
Changed drawers to hold their contents inside them, so what you put in a drawer slides out with it. Counters with a drawer are storage now.
Changed the mid-century fridges to keep only their bottom shelf, so the food storage sits on a clear tray, and moved the bookcases and shelves onto the mid-century set.
Changed smashed furniture to drop what it held on the floor just in front of it.

Changed doors and drawers to move under physics once pulled: they stay wherever you leave them, latch shut with a click when pushed home, and need another pull to open; stacked drawers no longer catch on each other.
Changed the Hardware Drawer to its own small steel cabinet with a top drawer that slides out, so its screws and dowels are stored in a drawer rather than a borrowed filing cabinet.

Changed how breakable furniture comes apart. It breaks into a handful of big chunks now instead of a scatter of crumbs and splinters, and a flat piece like a mat or a sign breaks into tiles rather than long thin plates.
Changed the crosshair to say when a piece is too heavy for your gloves, rather than offering a drag that barely shifts it.

Changed cars, toilets, cash registers, kilns, welding stations, hydroponics racks and wheelbarrow planters to plain furniture that no longer opens, and gave the repair station the crafting table's look.
Changed doors and drawers left open to slide shut on their own a moment after you walk away, so the store stays tidy.
Changed open shelving so it no longer holds a hidden container. Only furniture with a door or a drawer stores anything now.
Changed how furniture is placed so a piece faces you when you set it down, instead of turning its side or its back to you.
Changed storage and benches to open only from the front, and never while they are lying on their side.
Changed the hotbar to show your four weapon hooks and fade away when unused, so it only appears when it matters.
Changed health and stamina to show on your wristwatch in the bottom-left corner, so the screen stays clear.
Changed picked-up items to sit properly in the hand as they are carried to the pocket, each lined up to fit the palm and mirrored for the left hand, and no longer shrinking as they are grabbed.
Changed the basket screen to show your own character while you dress in armour, so you see exactly what you are wearing.
Changed the basket and cold bag to turn and face you on storage screens, with the weapon hooks on the outside of the basket's front wall.
Changed the basket and cold bag to sit square to you and tip toward the camera, and the basket's near wall now eases down so its contents show beside ovens and shelves.
Changed closing the basket beside furniture to ease the camera back to the player instead of cutting.
Changed scrap fabric and woven cloth to take a two-by-two space in the bag, so a bolt of cloth is not the size of a screw, and gave woven cloth a folded, hemmed shape of its own.
Changed dropped items so you can pick them up while they are still tumbling, instead of waiting for them to settle.
Changed the New Store screen to list the Durham store first and pick it by default.

Changed the corner minimap from a pocket compass to a little portable television, so the store reads as a picture on a curved tube rather than a dial - the glass bows the map and the markers are drawn large enough to pick out at a glance.
Changed mod scripting from JavaScript to Lua 5.4, and mods can now add or replace screens as JSON definitions.
Changed crouch-walking to 70% of walking speed, so sneaking is slower than walking.

Changed pinging to work like most games: tap the ping key to mark what you're looking at (an enemy, a teammate, a cupboard or a spot), or hold it for the ping wheel and release on Enemy, Loot, Go here or Danger.
Changed pings so you can have three up at once, plus one map waypoint, and ping one of your own again to remove it.
Changed the character previews in the Staff File and the inventory to live 3D views standing in a stockroom instead of a streamed picture, so they turn smoothly and read against a real setting.
Changed picking up, dropping and storing items to sound like what they are made of, and doors, drawers, stations, planters and vending machines make their own sounds too.

Changed the shopping trolley to a ten by four grid lying on the floor of its basket, and the weapon bench and stand mixer to one grid each. The stand mixer is cut open while you use it so you can see into the bowl.

Changed opening a counter or cabinet to slide its drawer out or swing its door open and lay the storage grid inside the drawer or on the shelf behind the door, so the contents sit where the piece keeps them rather than on its top.
Changed every menu, screen and HUD element to be drawn by the game itself instead of an embedded web browser. They look and work the same, without a browser running behind them.
Changed the store map to open with a softer hand, and both the map and the catalogue to lean very slightly away under the pointer, so paper held up answers the hand moving over it.

Changed the watch and the pocket television to drift a hair in the corner of the view and drag a moment behind a turn of the head, so they read as things carried rather than pictures stuck to the screen.
Changed the dot above furniture that opens a screen to half its size, with a softer edge.
Fixed boss summoner altars not standing on the floor.
Fixed the free-look camera bringing up the loading screen and hiding the world behind it.

Fixed an issue where every player shared one player number, so one player letting go of a saw or sewing machine stopped another player's work, and pings, name colours and spawn points could mix players up.
Fixed guests seeing lower ceilings than the host: the world data sent to joining players was missing the per-tile ceiling, difficulty and hazard layers, so every guest ceiling sat at the base height.
Fixed an issue where furniture the host had just moved, opened or damaged could vanish for everyone else and refuse to be dragged.
Fixed held weapons and picked-up items sitting outside the fist on the feminine body, and your own arms and held weapon dropping to a low-detail model up close on lower graphics settings.
Fixed punches on the feminine body: the fists now land where they should and the wrists are turned the right way, instead of following the masculine body's arms.
Fixed the two-handed slam on the feminine body, so the fists now meet with the wrists turned as animated instead of floating apart or sinking into each other.
Fixed turning with the right stick being faster at higher frame rates.
Fixed the first button press going missing after switching between mouse and controller, and held actions sticking on the switch.
Fixed an issue where the camera could stop turning with the mouse for the rest of the session after an attack that holds the camera on its target.
Fixed melee enemies running alongside a player who is holding an item without ever swinging; the held item was punching a hole in the navigation mesh under the player.
Fixed the male staff enemy standing in a T-pose.
Fixed fast travel refusing a teleporter far enough away that its part of the store had unloaded, reporting it as not found.
Fixed upper-body poses losing their aim while walking.
Fixed the hands drifting out of frame as you looked down, and the stretched look they had up close.

Fixed drawers and doors that jammed or hauled the whole cabinet when grabbed: a part now follows where you look, so a drawer pulls out as you look down its front and a door swings after the crosshair.

Fixed the blue fridge jumping sideways whenever it came to rest after a drag, and its doors refusing to be pulled: every rigged piece now shows the rig's own closed twin, so the still and moving shapes share one origin.
Fixed weapon hits on furniture and props spraying blood when the surface has no material of its own.
Fixed the mid-century chairs, sofas and shelves refusing to be dragged, an open door jumping when its piece was picked up or put down, and a red error line after closing a piece's screen mid-drag.
Fixed planks in the umbrella stand and boxes in the bike rack vanishing when the storage screen closed; they now stay on show after walking away and back and after a save and reload.
Fixed the inside of the fridges showing a dark diagonal patch and a stray shelf post where the upper shelves were removed.
Fixed open doors swinging loose while furniture is carried and snapping back when it lands, the oven door opening into the oven, and the oven drawer sitting too far out to grab.
Fixed fridge doors and drawers coming off their hinges, and opening an already-open fridge now carries on from where the door is.
Fixed things resting on a piece of furniture hanging in mid-air when it was dragged away, broken, taken apart or thrown.
Fixed switching a lamp or changing the contents of a piece you are carrying not taking effect until you put it down.
Fixed the screw and dowel boxes in the bag refusing to hand anything over: clicking an open box now takes out a single piece, which you can carry, drop or put back.
Fixed an issue where shift-clicking an item that had nowhere else to go moved it to the first empty spot in the basket.
Fixed the new British foods, sausages, rat meat and pigeon eggs floating at the palm when picked up; they now sit in the hand.
Fixed dropped items sinking into shelves or hanging in the air before they fall.
Fixed the map zooming two steps for each notch of the mouse wheel.
Fixed an issue where Escape did nothing on the Tab handbook, despite the panel saying it would close it. Escape and the gamepad Back button now close it as well as a second press of Tab.
Fixed the character editor showing clothes as a grey checkerboard instead of their real fabric.
Fixed ping markers missing their name and distance, not following enemies and teammates, and vanishing when behind you; they now stay on the edge of the screen.
Fixed an issue where saving within two seconds of joining or loading a game left out everything the player was carrying, so loading that save gave back an empty basket.
Fixed a smashed or dismantled teleporter staying on the map and in the fast-travel list, and a destroyed machine, cage, shop or planter keeping its old state in the save.

Fixed a dropped item or newly placed piece after loading a save sometimes taking over the identity of furniture in a part of the store that had not streamed in yet, so that furniture came back wrong or not at all.
Fixed furniture that was being dragged, falling, or ridden as a cart when the game saved vanishing on the next load.
Fixed the sewn cloth not appearing on the machine's bed once the seam was finished.
Fixed elevators never opening: calling one slid the cab's floor plates instead of its doors, so the doors stayed shut.
Fixed an issue where furniture a player had opened could vanish a moment later.
Fixed an issue where shelving, seating and display furniture was set too close together to fit, so pieces stood through each other. 322 spots across 50 store layouts.
Fixed an issue where bar stools and wide armchairs were set around dining tables, where they did not fit and clipped into each other.
Fixed an issue where items meant to be sitting on a table hung beside it or sank into it. They now settle onto whatever surface is under them.
Fixed an issue where bar stools, armchairs and office seating were set around dining tables. All of them had been marked as dining seating, so any of them could turn up at a table.

Fixed an issue where fridges, sofas, tables and machines spawned part-way through walls, racks and each other. Around a fifth of the furniture was built with its origin at a corner rather than under its middle, so it landed up to a metre from where the store layout meant to put it.
Fixed an issue where furniture spawned in mid-air over a stairwell. The staircases carried no collision at all, so nothing checked whether a piece was standing in one.
Removed the barefoot option from the shoes in character customisation. A character saved barefoot now wears the street trainers.
Removed the furnace, plastic extruder, plush machine, printer, pizza oven, rubbish compactor and plank rack for now.
Removed the higher tiers of the armour bench, crafting table, coffee machine, dishwasher, first aid station, microwave, oven, saw bench and sewing machine. Their recipes now craft on the first tier.

known_issues.text: Furniture flashes when a drag starts and again when it settles.
Elevators don't respond - pressing the button does nothing, so you can't ride between floors.
Some furniture spawns badly placed - floating near steps, lying down, or facing the wrong way.
Aisle sign lettering and framed photos z-fight at some angles - the text flickers as you walk past.
Railings generate along edges with no drop, and are missing from some real ones.
Standing beside a staircase, the ends of its steps show through the wall as a diagonal row of wooden strips climbing the next room's wall.
Some furniture turns flat grey once it is smashed, instead of keeping its colours.
The menus can feel sluggish and the cursor lags behind the mouse.
Very rarely a guest cannot pick up a piece of furniture that just appeared in front of them.
When friends join a loaded save, some rooms have a different ceiling height for them than for the host - and it is solid, so you can end up on different floors of the same room.
Some checkout counters and framed paintings flicker as you move - two surfaces are fighting over the same spot, not a missing texture.
Standing right next to a snail, it can't land a hit on you. Step back and it can kill you with its ranged attack.

entries.text: Changed the character preview to fill the whole stage instead of standing in a narrow portrait strip down the middle of it.
Changed drag-to-rotate on the character preview to turn the figure the way you drag, like pushing a turntable.
Fixed the dress shirt and knitted jumpers poking through the trousers they are tucked into, and showing skin just above the waistband. Each layer now keeps its own depth at the waist.
Fixed haircuts floating above some heads and the scalp showing through them on others, such as Lorenzo, Bruce and Walter. Each head now sets the hair at its own measured height.

Fixed trousers and belts showing through the hem of whichever top was worn over them. Each top and bottom was fitted only to its own outfit, so mixed pairs met at the waist; the bottoms now sit under every top and follow the hips with them.

Fixed the bought outfits' trousers and shorts showing a sliver of skin at the crotch. They were weighted to different bones than the skin under them, so the thigh came through whenever the doll stood with its legs apart.
Fixed the character editor showing clothes as a grey checkerboard instead of their real fabric.
